title: The 10-Minute Domain Fix: Stop Sending Cold Email From @gmail.com
description: Free Gmail addresses get about half the cold email replies. Set up a branded sending domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC in about 10 minutes.
lead: This is the full 10-minute fix from the reel. Hunter's data shows cold emails from a free address like @gmail.com get about half the replies of emails from a real business domain. Here's why, and exactly how to set up a proper sending domain, step by step, with the records to copy.
insider: Every client campaign we run sends from separate, branded domains with SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up, never from a free address and never from the client's main website domain. That setup sat under the campaign in the case study below: **236,545 emails in one quarter at a 3.69% reply rate, with 1,061 interested leads**. Buying one domain takes ten minutes. Running dozens of healthy domains and inboxes every day is what we do for clients.

blocks.text: What the data says

[Hunter's State of Email Outreach 2026](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email) looked at **31 million emails** sent by its users in 2025. Emails sent from a custom domain got a **5.2% reply rate**. Emails sent from free addresses got **2.5%**. That's a 108% difference, from one setting you choose before you write a single word.

blocks.text: "Spending a couple of dollars per month can effectively double your replies." ([Hunter, State of Email Outreach 2026](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email))
Why a free address costs you half your replies

items: **It looks like a stranger, not a business.** A buyer sees "sam@gmail.com" and can't tell who you work for. A real company domain answers that question before they open the email.

**You can't set up your own authentication.** SPF, DKIM and DMARC are records you add to a domain you own. On @gmail.com the domain belongs to Google, so you can't tune it for your sending. [Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) say authenticated messages are less likely to be rejected or marked as spam.
**Inbox filters are harsher.** Hunter says email providers may apply harsher spam filters to messages from free addresses.

**The limits are tiny.** A personal Gmail account can hit a limit at [more than 500 emails sent in a day](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/22839). Go over it and you can be blocked from sending for up to 24 hours.
**Google warns against it for bulk email.** Its guidelines list using an @gmail.com address for bulk email as a deceptive practice to avoid.

blocks.text: Worked example: same list, same email
You email **1,000** business owners with the same message. The only change is the sender address.

blocks.text: That's **27 extra conversations** from the same list and the same copy. 52 ÷ 25 = 2.08, so about twice the replies. No new leads, no new writing, just a different address.
The 10-minute fix, step by step

This is the setup for one sending domain with one inbox on Google Workspace. The clicks take about 10 minutes. DNS changes can take a little longer to show up everywhere, so do step 8 after a short wait.

items: **Pick a domain that looks like your brand.** If your website is acmeplumbing.com, try getacmeplumbing.com, acmeplumbinghq.com or tryacmeplumbing.com. Stick to .com when you can. **Never send cold email from your main website domain**: if it gets flagged, your normal business email suffers too.

**Buy it** at a registrar like [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/products/registrar/), [Namecheap](https://www.namecheap.com) or [GoDaddy](https://www.godaddy.com). It's a yearly fee, usually a few dollars a month.

**Create one inbox** with [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com) or [Microsoft 365](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/business). Use a real person's name: sam@getacmeplumbing.com, not sales@ or info@. Hunter found Google Workspace users had the highest average reply rate (**5.9%**), with Microsoft 365 at just over 4%.
**Add the SPF record** in your registrar's DNS settings. It tells inboxes which servers may send for your domain. Copy it from the box below.

**Turn on DKIM.** In the Google Admin console go to Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → Authenticate email, generate a 2048-bit key, add the TXT record it gives you, then click Start authentication. Google's [DKIM setup page](https://support.google.com/a/answer/180504) has screenshots.
**Add the DMARC record.** It tells inboxes what to do with mail that fails SPF or DKIM. Start with p=none, which Google allows, and get reports by email.
**Forward the new domain to your real website.** Prospects often check the domain before they reply. They should land on your actual site, not an empty page.

**Check your work.** Paste your domain into [Google Admin Toolbox Check MX](https://toolbox.googleapps.com/apps/checkmx/). Fix anything it flags. Then send a test email to a personal Gmail account, open it, click "Show original" and look for SPF: PASS, DKIM: PASS and DMARC: PASS.

blocks.text: The records to copy
Replace **yourdomain.com** with your new domain. These are for Google Workspace. If you use Microsoft 365, the SPF include is different (shown below).

blocks.label: DNS records for Google Workspace
blocks.text:
SPF
Type: TXT
Host/Name: @
Value: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all

DKIM
Type: TXT
Host/Name: google._domainkey
Value: (copy the long key from Google Admin > Gmail > Authenticate email)

DMARC
Type: TXT
Host/Name: _dmarc
Value: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com

Microsoft 365 SPF instead:
Value: v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all

blocks.label: Only one SPF record
blocks.text: A domain can have only **one** SPF record. If your sending tool also needs to be in SPF, add its include to the same line instead of creating a second record.
After the 10 minutes: don't send 500 emails on day one

A brand-new domain has no history. [Google's guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) say to start with a low volume and increase slowly, and to avoid sudden spikes like doubling what you sent before. Most cold email tools have a warm-up feature that does this for you. Use it, and be patient.

Once you're live, keep each inbox modest. Hunter found accounts sending **20 to 49 emails a day** got a **5.7% reply rate**, above the overall average of 4.5%. Need more volume? Add more inboxes and domains, don't push one inbox harder. Our [MATH guide](https://wayneflow.com/guides/math.html) shows how many you need for your goal.

blocks.text: Copy-paste prompt: find your sending domain

blocks.label: Paste into ChatGPT or Claude
blocks.text:
My company website is [yourcompany.com]. I need domain names for cold email that look like my brand but are separate from my main domain.

Give me 15 options using my brand name plus a short word (like get, try, hq, team, with). Rules:
- .com only
- under 20 characters before .com
- no hyphens, no numbers
- easy to read out loud
- nothing that looks like a misspelling or a fake version of another company

Rank them from most to least trustworthy-looking and say why in one short line each.
Check each name is free at your registrar, then buy one or two.
The 10-minute checklist

items: Domain bought, looks like my brand, not my main domain
One inbox with a real person's name
One SPF record
DKIM turned on and "Start authentication" clicked
DMARC record with p=none
Domain forwards to my real website
Check MX shows no errors, and a test email shows SPF, DKIM and DMARC: PASS
Warm-up turned on before any real sending

faq.q: Can I just use my main company email?
faq.a: For a few personal emails, yes. For cold outreach at any volume, no. Use separate look-alike domains so a problem never touches your main business email.

faq.q: How long until I can send real emails?
faq.a: The setup takes about 10 minutes. Then warm the inbox up and grow volume slowly, as Google recommends. Don't send a full campaign from a brand-new domain on day one.
Both work. In Hunter's data Google Workspace users had the highest average reply rate (5.9%), with Microsoft 365 just over 4%. Many senders use a mix.

faq.q: How many domains do I need?
faq.a: It depends on how many emails you want to send each day. Keep each inbox around 20-49 emails a day and add inboxes to grow. Our MATH guide walks through the numbers.
